ai.literal: Rain enduring, world functioning because of continuing, itself ambrosia that is to be understood.
ai.translation: Because the world continues to function only through the endurance of rain, rain itself is to be understood as the nectar of immortality.
ai.modern: மழை நிலைபெற்று பெய்வதால்தான் இந்த உலகம் தொடர்ந்து இயங்கி வருகிறது; ஆகையால் மழையே அமிழ்தம் என்று உணரத்தக்கது.
ai.explanation: This couplet establishes rain as the life-sustaining force of the earth. The word 'வான்' literally means sky, but in this context it stands for the rain that falls from it. The phrase 'நின்று வழங்கி வருதலால்' describes how the world continues to function and thrive because the rain endures and reliably provides for it. Because all earthly life depends entirely on this continuous cycle, rain itself ('தான்') is equated to 'அமிழ்தம்' (ambrosia), the mythical nectar of immortality. The concluding word 'உணரற்பாற்று' indicates that this is a fundamental truth of nature that one must realize.

ai.literal: To the eaters, having made food which became food, to the eaters, which became food also itself is rain.
ai.translation: Rain grows food for those who eat, and it also serves as food itself for those who eat.
ai.modern: உண்பவர்களுக்கு நல்ல உணவுகளை விளைவித்துத் தந்து, உண்பவர்களுக்குத் தானும் ஒரு உணவாக அமைவது மழையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the dual role of rain in sustaining life. The word துப்பு is used repeatedly here to mean food or that which is consumed. Rain first acts as the agent that grows crops, creating food for eaters. Then, as drinking water, rain becomes food itself, directly nourishing those who consume it.

ai.literal: Sky without if-fails, expanded-water vast world-in inside having-stood will-torment hunger.
ai.translation: If the rain from the sky fails, hunger will stay and torment even this vast world surrounded by the wide sea.
ai.modern: மழை பெய்யாமல் பொய்த்துவிட்டால், கடல் சூழ்ந்த இந்த அகன்ற உலகத்தின் உள்ளே பசி நிலைத்து நின்று உயிர்களைத் துன்புறுத்தும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute necessity of rain for survival. The phrase 'விரிநீர் வியனுலகத்து' describes the world as vast and surrounded by the expansive ocean. Despite having abundant seawater, the world cannot sustain life without fresh water from the sky ('விண்'). If the rain fails ('பொய்ப்பின்'), hunger ('பசி') will take root and continuously torment ('உடற்றும்') all living beings.

ai.literal: With the plough will not plough farmers, rain called income abundance having diminished if.
ai.translation: Farmers will not plough with their ploughs if the abundance of the income called rain diminishes.
ai.modern: மழை என்னும் வருவாய் தன் வளத்தில் குறைந்துவிட்டால், உழவர்கள் ஏரைக் கொண்டு நிலத்தை உழ மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that agriculture relies entirely on rainfall. The word 'வாரி' means income or revenue, portraying rain as the fundamental wealth that sustains the earth. If this natural income diminishes in its abundance, farmers cannot even begin their work with the plough, bringing all food production to a halt.

ai.literal: Ruining and, to the ruined having become a support, again just like that uplifting and, all (is) rain.
ai.translation: Rain is what ruins people by failing to fall, and rain is what uplifts the ruined by becoming their support.
ai.modern: பெய்யாமல் மக்களைக் கெடுப்பதும், அவ்வாறு கெட்டவர்களுக்குத் துணையாக இருந்து மீண்டும் அவர்களை வாழவைப்பதும் ஆகிய எல்லாம் மழையே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute power of rain over human prosperity. The word 'கெடுப்பதூஉம்' (ruining) refers to the devastation caused by droughts when rain fails. Conversely, 'எடுப்பதூஉம்' (uplifting) shows how the return of rain acts as a vital support to restore those very people. The elongated vowels in these two words are a poetic device (aḷapeṭai) that emphasizes the sheer magnitude of rain's dual capacity to both destroy and save.

ai.literal: From the sky drop if falls unless, otherwise there green grass head seeing is rare.
ai.translation: Unless drops of rain fall from the sky, it is rare to see even a blade of green grass.
ai.modern: வானத்திலிருந்து மழைத்துளி விழவில்லை என்றால், உலகத்தில் ஒரு பச்சைப் புல்லின் நுனியைக் கூடப் பார்ப்பது அரிது.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute necessity of rain for all life on earth. It states that without a single drop of rain falling from the sky, even the simplest form of life, a blade of green grass, cannot sprout or survive. The phrase 'பசும்புல் தலை' (head of green grass) vividly illustrates the smallest and most common vegetation. Thus, rain is shown as the fundamental source of life.

This shows that the ocean's fullness depends entirely on the continuous cycle of rain.

ai.literal: Special festivals and daily worship will not proceed, sky if it dries up, even for the celestials here.
ai.translation: If the heavens dry up, neither special festivals nor daily worship will be offered here on earth, even for the celestial beings.
ai.modern: மழை பெய்யாமல் வானம் வறண்டு போனால், இந்த உலகத்தில் தேவர்களுக்கும் திருவிழாக்களும் அன்றாடப் பூஜைகளும் நடைபெறாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute dependence of all earthly activities on rain, including the highest spiritual duties. The word வானம் (sky) stands for the rain it provides, and வறக்குமேல் means if it dries up. சிறப்பு refers to grand seasonal festivals, while பூசனை denotes regular daily worship. The verse states that without rain, human beings will lack the resources to perform even these sacred offerings to the celestial beings (வானோர்க்கும்) here on earth (ஈண்டு).

ai.literal: Charity, penance, both will not stay [in the] vast world, sky does not provide if.
ai.translation: If the heavens do not provide rain, neither charity nor penance will endure in this vast world.
ai.modern: வானம் மழையைத் தரவில்லை என்றால், இந்த அகன்ற உலகத்தில் தானம், தவம் ஆகிய இரண்டும் நிலைத்து நிற்கமாட்டா.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that all higher human virtues depend on the basic sustenance provided by nature. The word 'வானம்' literally means sky, but here it takes the accepted sense of the rain that the sky provides, which best fits the chapter's theme. The words 'தானம்' (charity) and 'தவம்' (penance) represent the two great moral duties: helping others and disciplining oneself. The phrase 'வியன் உலகம்' (vast world) highlights the scale of this dependence. If the sky fails to provide rain ('வழங்காது எனின்'), human beings will be too consumed by survival to practice these noble virtues, causing them to disappear from the world ('தங்கா').

ai.literal: Water without does not exist world if said, who to anyone sky without does not exist conduct.
ai.translation: If it is said that the world cannot exist without water, then for anyone at all, proper conduct cannot exist without the rain.
ai.modern: நீர் இல்லாமல் இந்த உலகம் அமையாது என்றால், மழை இல்லாமல் எவருக்கும் நல்லொழுக்கம் அமையாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet establishes the absolute necessity of rain for both physical survival and moral order. The word 'நீர்' (water) represents the basic element required for the world ('உலகு') to function. Just as the physical world cannot exist without water, the poet argues that 'ஒழுக்கு' (proper conduct or moral order) cannot be maintained by anyone ('யார் யார்க்கும்') without 'வான்' (the sky, meaning rain). Thus, rain is shown as the foundation of both life and virtue.
